biftu-quarry-mizan-dima-road.whole: At the credit's closing the Bank's completion report counts 305 km of the 434.5 km of road targeted as improved, rising to 320 km once the Mizan-Dima road was finished in April 2019: Kombolcha-Burka-Mille complete at 133 km, Mizan-Dima 77 km of 92, Konso-Yabello 95 km of 105, and the Ambo-Wolliso and Debre Birhan-Ankober contracts terminated. The share of rural land within 2 km of an all-season road rose from 17.8 to 36.9 per cent against a target of 40 per cent, 1,983,354 people were counted as beneficiaries against a target of 2,325,900, and average travel speed on the finished sections reached 70 km/h against a target of 80; travel and turnaround time for heavy goods vehicles on the Addis-Mille-Djibouti route stayed at six days, which the report attributes to the deterioration of the stretch inside Djibouti. The report's own after-the-fact calculation puts the Mizan-Dima road's economic rate of return at 32.4 per cent against 15.1 per cent estimated at appraisal; it says that figure is built from road agency costs and road users' vehicle operating and travel time costs over 20 years, so it measures nothing paid to anyone moved or compensated. All of these are the Bank's own figures; its Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, reviewed them in January 2020 and agreed with the completion report's Moderately Unsatisfactory outcome rating. No independent check was found.
biftu-quarry-mizan-dima-road.searched: World Bank WDS document list for P117731; the Implementation Completion and Results Report of 23 September 2019 (Ethiopia-Transport Sector-Project.pdf) and the Independent Evaluation Group's ICR Review of 28 January 2020 (Ethiopia-Ethiopia-Transport-Sector-Project.pdf), both downloaded with curl and read from disk with pdftotext. The two documents agree on the road lengths and the rating; they differ by rounding on the baseline travel speed (25 km/h in the completion report's table, 23 km/h in the review) and on the rural access index (36.9 against 37 per cent). No non-Bank account of what the roads delivered was found.

caldwell-bridge-liberia-compensation.whole: The Bank's completion report counts 24 km of Monrovia city streets and 148.5 km of rural road on the Cotton Tree-Buchanan and Pleebo-Barclayville corridors rehabilitated, a new road intersection at the Vai Town Bridge, and maintenance on 45.5 km of previously repaired rural road against an original target of 641 km, the shortfall following the cancellation of two misprocured lots; a new fuel unloading facility at the Port of Monrovia was built but was not yet in service when the project closed. Average travel time between Cotton Tree and Buchanan fell from 163 minutes to 55, and between Pleebo and Barclayville from 160 to 45; the share of Monrovia streets rated good or fair went from 5 to 35 per cent, and 94 per cent of the rural population was recorded as living within reach of an all-season road. The report puts the number of people who benefited at 1,194,729 against a revised target of 744,980, counted by drawing a 10 km band around the roads and assuming the whole population of Monrovia gained from the urban works. It gives an economic rate of return of 18 per cent, covering 86 per cent of project cost, with none calculated at appraisal. All the figures are the Bank's own; its Independent Evaluation Group, the Bank's internal evaluators, kept the report's Satisfactory outcome rating but lowered its rating of the Bank's own performance from Highly Satisfactory to Satisfactory, citing shortcomings in monitoring. No independent check was found.

chebei-village-guangzhou-resettlement.whole: The project built or expanded three domestic wastewater treatment plants in Guangzhou with a combined capacity of 475,000 cubic metres a day, which the Bank's completion report says took the share of the city's wastewater that is treated from 50 to 97 per cent against a target of 90 per cent, and which the Independent Evaluation Group puts at about a fifth of Guangzhou's treatment capacity. A hazardous waste treatment facility was enlarged during construction from a planned 150,000 to 290,000 cubic metres; it was not running when the completion report was written, began operating in August 2013 under a three-year private contract, and had treated about 9,000 tonnes by the time the review was posted, against the report's target of 45,000 tonnes a year. Average sewerage tariffs rose about 50 per cent, from Rmb 0.70 to Rmb 1.07 per cubic metre, against a project target of Rmb 1.50 and an estimated Rmb 2.94 needed to cover operating costs and depreciation. Spending reached US$520.8 million against US$431.9 million estimated at appraisal, the increase met entirely by the government, and no economic rate of return was calculated at appraisal or at completion. Both documents are the Bank's, and they disagree: the completion report rated the outcome Moderately Satisfactory, while the Independent Evaluation Group rated it Moderately Unsatisfactory, noting that the project's investments amounted to about 6 per cent of the US$8.5 billion the government was spending at the same time on the Pearl River clean-up, that only two of three planned inter-municipal pilots were completed and the regional master plan was not implemented, and that improvements in river water samples (about 70 per cent meeting Class III against a 58 per cent baseline and an 80 per cent target) cannot be attributed to the project. No independent check was found.

cuijiaying-han-river-resettlement.whole: The complex carries six turbines with 90 MW of installed capacity, which the Bank's completion report says generated 431 GWh in 2010 with about 446 GWh expected in a normal year, and which it equates to about 322,800 tonnes of carbon dioxide avoided; the dam adds roughly 40 million tonnes of live storage for Xiangfan municipality and for 118,000 hectares of irrigated land in the Tangdong farmland region. Thirty-three kilometres of waterway upstream of the complex were improved so that vessels of up to 1,000 tonnes and tows of two to four barges can use them, lock availability reached 95 per cent against a target of 85, and the project team told the Independent Evaluation Group that inland waterway traffic in the Xiangfan area was 5.61 million tonnes in 2010 against 3.66 million tonnes in the 2003 base year. Spending came to US$254.2 million against US$211.1 million estimated at appraisal, and the report's economic rate of return was 21.3 per cent at completion against 22.2 per cent estimated at appraisal, covering 99 per cent of project cost. Every figure is the Bank's or its borrower's; on the project's claim that income per head in the dam area rose from just over 3,000 yuan before the project to over 5,000 yuan in 2010, the Independent Evaluation Group notes that the figure comes from the borrower's own survey of resettled families, with no counterfactual and no indication of whether it is adjusted for inflation, and it lowered the report's Satisfactory outcome rating to Moderately Satisfactory because the evidence on living standards was insufficient. No independent check was found.

guiguang-railway-land-acquisition.whole: The line was built: 847 km of double-track electrified passenger railway from Guiyang to Guangzhou, with 342 bridges and viaducts and 233 tunnels, and 21 stations against a target of 30. The Bank's completion report says average travel time between the two ends fell from 1,500 minutes to 251, an 83 per cent cut that beat the original target of 330 minutes, and that express passenger trains went from three pairs a day to 25; it was decided not to run freight on the line, so the added capacity is for passengers only. A survey of 467 passengers on 12 trains at closing found 61 per cent travelling as tourists and 36 per cent on business, over 40 per cent with monthly incomes of 4,000 yuan or less, and 36 per cent saying they would not have made the trip without the line. The Bank's US$299.5 million loan sat inside a project costed at US$12.53 billion at appraisal and US$13.05 billion at closing, a unit cost of about US$14 million per kilometre that the report calls among the lowest in the world; the report's economic rate of return was 18 per cent at completion against 16 per cent at appraisal, covering 74 per cent of project cost and built from travel time and distance savings, freed capacity on existing lines, and fewer road accidents and emissions. All the figures are the Bank's own, and the two Bank documents differ on the verdict: the completion report rated the outcome Highly Satisfactory, the Independent Evaluation Group Satisfactory, and the group also raised the risk to the outcome from Negligible to Modest over the new line's financial viability. No independent check was found.

guiyang-youxiao-road-resettlement.whole: The project built 7.04 km of urban road designed for 60 km/h, 11 stretches of rural road, 15 rural bus terminals and a freight depot. The Bank's completion report says Youxiao Road cut travel between the Longdongbao area and downtown Guiyang, which a mountain had separated from the city centre, and the project team told the Independent Evaluation Group the saving was 21 minutes; in the rural area 67 more administrative villages were linked by all-weather roads, the new bus terminals serve 118 villages, and a survey covering a quarter of the project's rural roads found average travel time on them down from 39.8 to 25.8 minutes. The report also credits the road with drawing Rmb 528 million of investment into Bixiang Town after it opened in 2013, a 192 per cent rise on 2009, and a 129.2 per cent rise in that township's revenue. Spending reached US$360.7 million against US$314.4 million estimated before appraisal, and the report's economic rate of return was 16 per cent at completion against 16.9 per cent at appraisal, covering over 99 per cent of project cost. Every figure here is the Bank's own; the Independent Evaluation Group agreed with the report's Moderately Satisfactory outcome rating but rated the quality of the report itself Unsatisfactory and raised the risk to the outcome from Moderate to Significant, because rural road maintenance funding was still short. No independent check was found.

himachal-pradesh-state-roads-debris.whole: Alongside the upgraded roads, the Bank's completion report counts periodic maintenance on 1,831 km against a target of 2,000 km, 25 accident blackspots treated against a target of 20, and a road accident database running in every district of the state by July 2015. It says average speeds on the upgraded roads rose from 29 to 40 km/h, an increase of 38 per cent against a 25 per cent target, that the share of the state's core network in poor condition fell from 40 per cent to 10.4 per cent, and that deaths in traffic accidents per 1,000 vehicles fell from 0.28 in 2014 to 0.21 in 2017. No outcome indicator for transport costs was set when the project was appraised, so a proxy was used at closing: average vehicle operating cost of 9.78 rupees per kilometre against a pre-project 14.39, a 32 per cent reduction. The state did not create the road fund the project had planned, and the share of in-house labour in maintenance spending fell only from 75 to 62 per cent against a 50 per cent target. All these figures are the Bank's; the report's economic rate of return was 26 per cent at completion against 27 per cent at appraisal, covering 88 per cent of project cost, and the Independent Evaluation Group, while agreeing with the Moderately Satisfactory outcome rating, rated the project's efficiency Modest in spite of that return because of the cost and time overruns, and cut the rating of the project's monitoring from Substantial to Modest. No independent check was found.

huai-river-flood-drainage-resettlement.whole: The Bank's completion report counts 444.62 km of dikes built against a target of 417.45 km, 1,023.51 km of river dredged against 980.54 km, 252 irrigation and drainage pumping stations against 182, 487 sluice gates and culverts against 427, 250 bridges against 197, 140.88 km of drainage ditches dug or rehabilitated, and 36 farmer-run flood diversion and irrigation associations set up. It reports 9,682.4 square kilometres of rural and urban land protected from flooding against a target of 9,576.2, and 7.43 million people protected against a target of 6.54 million. Incomes were recorded as improved for 81,311 affected people against a target of 57,173; agricultural income per head rose by RMB 260 a year against a target of RMB 233; commerce across the four provinces grew by RMB 263.33 million against a target of RMB 118.41 million; and flood-related losses of crops and property fell by RMB 797.99 million against a target of RMB 699.45 million. The Bank's US$200 million loan sat inside a project costed at US$597.41 million, and the report's economic rate of return was 25 per cent at completion against 20 per cent at appraisal, covering 61 per cent of project cost. All the figures are the Bank's own; the Independent Evaluation Group agreed with every rating in the report, and recorded that the report's further claim that losses fell because flood control let people diversify into aquaculture was not documented. No independent check was found.

jituhun-railway-resettlement.whole: The line was built: 360 km of double-track electrified passenger railway from Jilin to Hunchun designed for 250 km/h, with 90.96 km of track on bridges and viaducts, 155.7 km inside 66 tunnels, and a 3.3 km four-track bridge over the Songhua River; six of the eight planned stations were commissioned when the project closed. The Bank's completion report says transit time between Tumen and Jilin fell from 420 minutes to 113, that train pairs a day on the corridor rose to 26 against a target of 13, and that the line carried 8.2 million passengers past a fixed measuring point against a target of 8 million. It also records that traffic density in 2016 was about 24 per cent below the appraisal estimate, and a survey of 500 passengers found 17 per cent who would not have travelled without the line and 83 per cent who would have used another mode. The Bank's US$198.7 million loan sat inside a project costed at US$6.30 billion; the report's economic rate of return was 8.4 per cent at completion against 6.2 per cent at appraisal, counting only the time passengers save against road and existing rail. All the figures are the Bank's own, and the two Bank documents differ on the verdict: the completion report rated the outcome and the borrower's performance Highly Satisfactory, while the Independent Evaluation Group rated both Satisfactory, on the ground that passenger demand came in below the appraisal estimate and two stations were unfinished. No independent check was found.

karnataka-state-highways-ii-compensation.whole: The Bank's completion report counts 831 km of Karnataka's core road network widened to two lanes against a revised target of 845 km, 503 km of it under ordinary contracts and 300 km under ten-year design-build-finance-operate-maintain-transfer concessions, with 19 km left unfinished at closing over land acquisition; a further 1,078 km of non-rural roads were rehabilitated as planned. It reports travel time on the project roads down 30 to 40 per cent against a target of 25 per cent, vehicle operating costs down 19 per cent against 15 per cent, and the share of the state's classified road network in good or fair condition up from 50 to 70 per cent. On the 62 km road safety demonstration corridor the report records deaths down 41 per cent against a target of 21 per cent and 143 accident blackspots treated in 2018-19; it gives the fall in accidents as 60 per cent in one passage and 66 per cent in another. The state raised US$416.5 million from private lenders against a revised target of US$400 million and an original target of US$500 million; the state road development corporation mobilised about US$97 million of that, which the report puts at about 60 per cent of the construction cost of the concession roads, the rest coming from the Bank loan and a commercial bank. The project generated about 0.83 million days of unskilled work, 69 per cent of it going to local workers and 17 per cent to women. All these figures are the Bank's own; the report's economic rate of return was 32 per cent at completion against 30 per cent at appraisal, covering 97 per cent of project cost and built from vehicle operating cost savings, travel time savings and lower maintenance costs, and the Independent Evaluation Group agreed with every rating in the report. No independent check was found.

liaoning-medium-cities-resettlement.whole: Across the six municipalities the Bank's completion report counts 107 km of road and six bridges built or rebuilt - less than planned because the local governments did some stretches with their own money - about 4,478,000 square metres of road surface and footway repaired, traffic lights along 156 km, drainage along 107 km, 824 traffic monitoring and control installations, 141 sets of maintenance equipment, and for public transport 20 bus priority routes, 11 depots, 196 stops and shelters and 112 buses in Panjin. It reports travel times on 12 monitored routes down by between 13 and 68 per cent, the share of city roads in good condition up from a range of 41 to 60 per cent before the project to 70 to 89 per cent after, bus passenger numbers up by between 21 per cent in Fushun and 281 per cent in Panjin, and traffic deaths per 10,000 vehicles down by between 15 per cent in Liaoyang, from 3.3 to 2.8, and 70 per cent in Jinzhou, from 4.3 to 1.3. One part of the project largely did not happen: only Jinzhou put road maintenance out to competitive tender, the other cities used limited bidding with municipally owned companies, and the Independent Evaluation Group rated that objective Modest, finding no evidence that maintenance costs or coverage improved. Spending came to US$397.4 million against US$525.4 million estimated at appraisal, and the report's economic rate of return was 22.7 per cent at completion against 15.2 per cent at appraisal, though the later figure covers only 41 per cent of project cost against 70 per cent for the appraisal estimate. All the figures are the Bank's own, and the Independent Evaluation Group agreed with the report's Satisfactory outcome rating. No independent check was found.

liuzhan-railway-resettlement.whole: The project double-tracked and upgraded the existing single-track electrified railway between Liupanshui and Zhanyi, across three mountain ranges. The Bank's completion report counts 97 km of track laid in Guizhou, including 62.3 km of tunnel and 15.7 km of bridge and viaduct, with two new and seven rebuilt stations, and 99.7 km in Yunnan, including 10.7 km of tunnel and 9.2 km of bridge. It reports freight train speeds up from 23 to 70 km/h against a target of 41, express passenger speeds up from 55 to 100 km/h against a target of 90, and trains up from 31 to 45 pairs a day by October 2014, four months after the loan closed, against a target of 50 pairs after the first full year. Spending came to US$1,541.6 million against US$1,120.2 million estimated at appraisal, 40 per cent more, which the report attributes to higher construction costs, change orders and the renovation of 14 stations that had not been costed; its economic rate of return was 13 per cent at completion against 17 per cent at appraisal, covering the whole project. All these figures are the Bank's own, and the Independent Evaluation Group agreed with the report's Satisfactory outcome rating. No independent check was found.
